import pandas as pd

# Load source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
source0_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_54/training_0.csv"
source1_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_54/training_1.csv"

df0 = pd.read_csv(source0_path, index_col=0)
df1 = pd.read_csv(source1_path, index_col=0)

# Operation 1: JOIN Source2_54_0 and Source2_54_1 on "ID"
df_joined = pd.merge(df0, df1, on="ID", how="inner")

# Operation 2: group_by sex (from Source2_54_1.sex) and aggregate avg of G1, G2, G3 (from Source2_54_0)
# Note: After join, columns G1, G2, G3 come from df0, sex comes from df1
grouped = df_joined.groupby("sex").agg({
    "G1": "mean",
    "G2": "mean",
    "G3": "mean"
}).reset_index()

# Rename columns to match target schema exactly (sex: string, G1/G2/G3: float)
# The aggregation already produces float columns
grouped = grouped[["sex", "G1", "G2", "G3"]]

# Write the result to the target path
target_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_54/target_multisource.csv"
grouped.to_csv(target_path, index=False)

import pandas as pd

# Read source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the first numerical index column
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_54/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_54/training_1.csv", index_col=0)

# Join on ID
joined = pd.merge(source0, source1, on="ID", how="inner")

# Group by 'sex' and aggregate averages of G1, G2, G3
result = joined.groupby("sex", as_index=False).agg({
    "G1": "mean",
    "G2": "mean",
    "G3": "mean"
})

# Ensure columns are exactly as target schema and types
result = result.astype({
    "sex": str,
    "G1": float,
    "G2": float,
    "G3": float
})

# Write output
result.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_54/target_multisource_critique_history.csv", index=False)
